key_insight: Whole-genome sequencing in Latin American early-onset/familial Parkinson’s cases uncovered a meaningful burden of actionable genetic variants that standard array-based screening could miss.
clinical_relevance: These findings support broader genomic testing for selected Parkinson’s patients in Latin America to improve identification of monogenic disease and related risk variants.
method: Cohort: 263 individuals with early-onset and/or family-history-positive Parkinson’s disease from LARGE-PD.
Sequencing targeted seven PD genes plus 21 genes linked to related parkinsonian disorders.
evidence_signal: In the analyzed cohort, 4.7% had pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants in primary/secondary PD genes, 5.5% had pathogenic/likely pathogenic Gaucher disease variants, and 2.7% carried known GBA1 risk variants.
watch_item: The sequencing subset included only individuals without known pathogenic PD variants on prior genotyping, so the yield and variant spectrum may not generalize to all Parkinson’s patients or settings.
paper_title: Genomic Landscape of Early-Onset and Familial Latin American Parkinson's Patients
